reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the formation of a MoO₂ lubricating layer and the claimed friction and wear reductions in (AlCrTiZrMoₓ)N coatings. However, the hypothesis extends these findings to a different class of materials (bulk, non-nitride HEAs such as CoCrFeMnNi) without any cited evidence for such systems, and the specific Mo concentration range (10–15 at.%) is not validated by the cited study, which varied Mo content without specifying an optimum. E2 provides only general background on friction and does not support any specific premise.
premises: Mo addition to a nitride HEA coating reduces friction from ~0.72 to ~0.26 and wear rate by 10×
The friction reduction is due to formation of a MoO₂ lubricating layer during sliding
The MoO₂ layer forms because of frictional heat at the wear track
The effect is demonstrated in (AlCrTiZrMoₓ)N coatings with varying Mo content
The proposed mechanism (shear-able MoO₂ tribolayer) is directly transferable to bulk HEAs like CoCrFeMnNi
